name: Estimated from G.H2 Production with CO2 balance
notes:
The emission factors are for non-combustion emissions in central plants from NA NG to G.H2 production. Unit is g/mmBtu NG input

The formulas in these EFs reflect the change in option of H2 production assumptions in process "Option: H2 Producion Assumptions (H2A model or Industrial data)" (id=212338942). Unless fully understand the meanings of the formulas, do not modify them. 

This technology is created to account the emissions used in the G.H2 central plant production processes, in which these emission items are defined at per mmbtu G.H2 produced.  It is created to serve as the base of non-combustion emissions based on G.H2 Production, which is defined with constant emission factors in Hydrogen!$C$69~C74."

Because the process efficiencies vary from year to year and from with co-product to without co-product, and because we assumed any NG beyond the 1mmbtu in the feed is counted as feed loss, we can define this technology in such a way that as long as it is applied to 1mmbtu NG feed (which together with the process fuels produces the 1mmbtu G.H2), the emissions will be calculated as constants per 1mmbtu G.H2 production at central plants. Or, when used in other processes, such as MeOH, Oil Sand, G.H2 production at refueling stations, we could define a time-series for the efficiency ratio of the G.H2 central plant production vs. the corresponding (MeOH, Oil Sand, G.H2 produciton at refueling station) processes. 

For example, when used in processes that produce MeOH, Oil Sand, G.H2, etc. from NG, we need to consider the time-varying technology shares while using this constant emission factor set.
